subFeatures.heading: One QR code, a menu in 35 languages.
subFeatures.body: Guests scan the QR and pick their language: the translation is done by AI with culinary sensibility, not a generic translator. No more separate tourist menus or scattered sheets on the table.
bullets: One printed QR covers 35 languages, included in the subscription.
The AI speaks the language of food — dish names sound natural in every language.
Guests switch languages inside the menu, without rescanning the QR.

subFeatures.heading: Allergens and dietary labels inside the QR menu.
subFeatures.body: Every dish in the menu behind the QR can carry labels: gluten, lactose, nuts, seafood, vegan and gluten-free options. Guests filter dishes to their restrictions from their phone, without asking the staff.
bullets: 14 allergen categories at the dish level.
Vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free labels with one click in the panel.
Guests filter the QR menu by their own restrictions.

subFeatures.heading: A QR menu styled like a restaurant website.
subFeatures.body: After scanning the code, guests don't land on a flat PDF: they see a welcome screen with a video or striking photo, a description of the venue and a contact page with a map, phone numbers and social links. The QR becomes your restaurant's front door online.
bullets: A background video or striking photo on the QR menu start screen.
Room to tell the story of your venue and each category.
A built-in contact page: map, phone, Instagram, WhatsApp.

image.alt: Two phones on a table: the QR menu start screen with a background video and a contact page with a map

subFeatures.heading: From the QR code, guests can order too.
subFeatures.body: Beyond browsing the menu, the QR menu can become an ordering channel: guests add dishes to the cart and send the request. The order reaches a waiter on the floor, your WhatsApp or the kitchen screen. The feature can be switched on and off in settings whenever needed.
bullets: A cart, comments and order submission straight from the QR scan.
The order instantly reaches the floor, WhatsApp or the kitchen screen.
Enable the feature by hours, floors or specific restaurants.

faq.sub: What restaurateurs ask about the IQ Rest QR menu. Can't find your question? Message us on WhatsApp.

items.q: How does the IQ Rest QR menu work?
items.a: Every table has a printed QR code. Guests scan it with their phone camera, and the browser opens the restaurant's menu — photos, descriptions, allergens and up-to-date prices. No app to download for guests or staff.

items.q: Do I need technical skills to create a QR menu?
items.a: No. The panel works with clicks and drag-and-drop, no code or complex configuration. Adding a dish takes seconds: name, price, photo. Initial setup usually takes 30 minutes to an hour; if you already have a PDF menu, AI converts it automatically.

items.q: Do guests need to install an app to read the QR?
items.a: No. The built-in iPhone and Android camera recognizes the QR code in seconds and opens the menu right in the browser. The admin panel also works in any modern browser — phone, tablet or laptop.

items.q: How are the table QR codes printed?
items.a: QR codes are generated automatically in the panel (one per table or one for the whole venue) and downloaded as a print-ready PDF. An office printer and a stand are all you need: a holder, a sticker or a coaster.

items.q: Can I use my own domain for the QR menu?
items.a: Yes. We support your restaurant's domain with an SSL certificate (for example menu.yourrestaurant.com): when guests scan the QR, they see your restaurant's address, not a generic subdomain. DNS setup takes 5–10 minutes and we guide you through it.

items.q: Can I manage QR codes for several restaurants from one account?
items.a: Yes, on request. One account can bring together several venues, each with its own QR codes, menu, design and analytics. Message us on WhatsApp and we'll enable multi-restaurant mode.

items.q: Is it hard to launch a QR menu from scratch?
items.a: Three steps: (1) create categories; (2) add dishes with a name, price and photo; (3) print the QR codes and place them on the tables. If you already have a paper menu or a PDF, upload it — AI recognizes categories and prices and fills in the cards. A basic menu can be online in 5 minutes.

finalCta.heading: A QR menu in 10 minutes.
finalCta.sub: No card needed, cancel anytime. Trusted by {count} restaurants. Just an email — and no apps for your guests.
